resources.string: gig.log uses Android\'s Accessibility service to read the screens of the delivery apps you turn on. It reads offers aloud while you drive and records your shifts, deliveries and pay. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. With Screen events on, it also sees which other app is open. It drops recognized screens with your banking, payment or ID details, the ID camera and the signature pad without saving anything, and saves customer names and addresses in your history only as codes. If you turn on screenshots, it can save a picture of the whole screen, with everything on it. It taps a delivery app\'s button only when you press Accept or Decline in gig.log, or for an automatic tap you allow. This test build saves the text of the delivery apps\' screens. On screens it recognizes, its rules replace the customer details they know about; elsewhere the filters can miss them. Its log keeps screen text too. Census upload, off unless turned on in developer options, sends outlines of unrecognized screens, counts showing which screens gig.log recognizes and the app version, with this install\'s ID. Capture sharing, also off unless turned on, needs census upload and the server\'s trust, and sends the text of unrecognized screens, which the server\'s operator can read. Spoken offers go to your phone\'s text-to-speech engine, which may use the network. Android backup and exports you make can copy your history.

gig.log skips every other app\'s notifications without reading them. What it recognizes is saved in your history. This test build also saves notification text, and census upload, off unless turned on in developer options, can send outlines of notifications gig.log doesn\'t recognize.
